Subject: Re: CortexAI pilot — tech note (batching, cache, quant)

Team — rough tech summary for CortexAI (keeps it short for the customer):

Core assumptions:
- Target model: 13B chat model (structure similar to MPT/GPT-style causal stacks)
- Typical request seq length: 64 tokens (avg) with occasional 512-token long form
- Traffic shape: spiky; warm steady-state for 2–3 hours/day

Recommendations / expected outcomes:
1) Continuous batching (window 50–100ms): p50 token latency improvement ~15–25% vs single-request path; p95 improvement more modest (~8–12%) due to tail scheduling. Good fit for Cortex's concurrent pattern.
2) KV prefix caching (session affinity): expect ~30–45% token reduction for repeated prompt patterns (chat histories). Important to size RAM: 2–3GB per 100k active sessions for a compact kv schema.
3) Quantization: start with mixed float16 + int8 for dense layers (safe baseline) — expect 10–18% cost reduction vs fp16 with <1% quality delta on summarization tasks. AWQ/4-bit aggressive path shows 30–45% cost wins but requires validation on your eval set; potential quality regression in edge cases.
4) Ops caveats: cold-starts will temporarily reduce batching effectiveness; pre-warming and keeping a small reserved pool for the pilot reduces that risk.

Suggested pilot config to communicate:
- Model variant: 13B fp16 baseline; int8 opt-in for steady-state runs; AWQ-4 reserved for optional A/B test
- Runtime knobs: batching window 75ms, per-session KV cache TTL 24h, reserve 1 GPU slot for steady-state warm pool
- Expected net token-cost reduction (conservative): 25–35% with batching + KV + int8

Attaching a short markdown with the micro-bench numbers.

—Aditya
